text:
kevin: Hey team — received GCP's revised EDP. They pushed back on a hard H100 guarantee but offered a 'safety stock' burst pool. Sharing highlights and questions.

anya: Can you paste the key paragraphs? We should check true-up windows and how they meter preemptible / spot.

maria: Quick note — our baseline ask was 500k GPU-hours across H100/A100 over 12 months with a 20% burst buffer and regional carveouts for eu-west1.

kevin: Paste from the vendor: 
```
Commitment: Customer commits to purchase aggregate compute units equivalent to 500,000 GPU-hours (H100 equiv) over a 12-month term.
Burst: Vendor will provide a transient burst pool up to 15% of committed capacity subject to regional availability. Burst access is best-effort; no SLA.
True-up: Monthly true-up, billed at committed rate for shortfalls.
Preemption: Preemptible instances are excluded from commitment unless named in a separate appendix.
Metering: Vendor reserves right to adjust metering mapping for fractional GPU usage; disputes to be raised within 60 days.
```

sam: That "best-effort" burst pool is not acceptable — we need defined minimum burst (at least 5% guaranteed) for queued inference spikes. Also we should avoid monthly true-ups billed at the committed rate for shortfalls; makes us overpay during onboarding.

kevin: Agreed. Proposed counterpoints: 1) Long-term: Replace "best-effort" with "guaranteed burst floor of 5% per region, additional best-effort up to 15%." 2) True-up: Quarterly true-up with roll-forward credit for overages/shortfalls (so usage variance evens out). 3) Metering disputes: extend window to 120 days and require vendor to provide per-instance metering logs on request.

anya: Also push on SKU carveouts. If they mix A100/H100 equivalency we need a conversion table with per-SKU multipliers. Otherwise billing opacity kills our cost models. Example conversion line: `1 H100_80GB = 1.0 unit, 1 A100_80GB = 0.6 unit`

maria: Add clause for preemption protection on critical routes: any preemption rate >3% in a calendar month triggers automatic fallback to dedicated pool or an SLA credit.

dev-bot: deploy-bill-checker: latest usage shows 42% of our steady jobs ran on preemptible instances last month due to autoscaler config — likely skews the commitment math. https://internal/reports/edp-usage-march.pdf

kevin: Important — vendor will want our forecast. I propose we offer a ramp schedule: Q1 20%, Q2 35%, Q3 70%, Q4 100% of committed baseline. This buys us time while we move inference to dedicated routing.

sam: For negotiating leverage, ask them for: 1) a three-month suspension clause if we face a sustained preemption wave; 2) a price ladder that discounts with utilization tiers; 3) a one-time onboarding credit equal to 2% of the first-year commitment for migration costs.

anya: Finance will want a reconciliation playbook in the contract: invoice format, CPI (cloud price index) pass-through caps, remediation timeline, and a standing review cadence every 90 days. Without that we can't accept their metering "reserve right" clause.

maria: Can someone draft the counters in legal-friendly language? I can take the burst/region carveouts. kevin — can you own metering and true-up wording? anya — finance bits? sam — commercial concessions (credits/ladder)?

kevin: I'll draft metering + true-up. Two specific ask bullets I want in wording: 
1) Vendor must provide per-request resource logs for disputed months within 14 days.
2) Any change in metering methodology requires 90-day notice and explicit opt-out for existing commitments.

sam: Also, request a separate appendix for "Emergency Capacity Guarantee" — for a fee we get guaranteed dedicated warm pool for a bounded time (up to 72 hours) with defined ramp-up time and IP/networking adjacency constraints. This helps us for launches.

anya: Great. Maria — let's get a short financial model showing how the ramp + burst floor affects effective $/token and $/hour. I'll present to CFO Thursday.

maria: Will do. I'll include two scenarios: conservative (no guaranteed burst) vs negotiated burst floor + ladder.

kevin: Ok team — I'll upload the draft counters in #vendors-docs by EOD. If anyone wants to add legal phrasing DM me.

sam: One last ask — flag any clauses that waive vendor liability for network egress or cross-region replication. We must keep data transfer credits explicit.

kevin: noted. Closing loop after draft. :thumbsup:
